newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower Monday, pressured by lighter demand as packers start cutting back on slaughter, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant Monday could range from $58.50 to $59.50. Top prices Friday ranged from $59.00 to $60.50.
Illinois top prices Monday could range from $58.50 to $59.00 at the plant, depending on how many hogs are marketed, dealers said. Top prices Friday at the plant were $59.00.
Indiana buyers said top hog prices Monday at the plant could range from $58.00 to $58.50, unchanged from Friday.

Most packers were planning on reducing hog slaughter next week in an attempt to mend slipping operating margins, the dealers said. Margins late this week reportedly were eroded by higher cash hog prices and weak pork prices.
Carlot pork prices at midday were steady for hams and lower for pork bellies amid light demand and offerings.
